sections.title: A steady place to make sense of what you are carrying
paragraphs: Hi, I’m Amanda (she/her). I’m a **Registered Clinical Counsellor** (license #29097) with the BC Association of Clinical Counsellors.

While my counselling work currently focuses on eating disorder recovery and disordered eating, including anorexia, bulimia, orthorexia, binge eating, and body image concerns, I also welcome clients who may be looking for support with anxiety, depression, life transitions, self-worth, and burnout.

Early on in my undergraduate degree, I had the pleasure of meeting people in eating disorder recovery. They shared their stories with me, describing the isolation and stigma they felt and the lack of resources available to help them in their recovery.

Hearing their stories and witnessing their resilience and vulnerability inspired me to volunteer with a local non-profit, **Looking Glass Foundation**, to help increase access to mental health support for those in eating disorder recovery. I deeply cherished my time there, so I returned as a practicum student during my graduate program to deepen my skill set.

I am truly passionate about this work. I have seen people make incredible strides in their recovery, from their eating disorder completely running the show to thriving and leading healthy lives aligned with who they are at their core, not the eating disorder. They have shown me and others that **recovery is possible**.

sections.title: My Approach
paragraphs: I take a **collaborative**, **holistic**, and **trauma-informed** approach to counselling, striving to meet each person with warmth, empathy, non-judgement, and a desire to truly understand their unique experiences. Clients have shared that they also appreciated my authenticity, playfulness, and willingness to help them stay accountable throughout our work together.

My intention is to deeply listen and hold space for you while showing up as my **authentic self**, not a blank slate or robot. In our work together, I may bring my humanness into the room, like my genuine reactions, when it feels therapeutically releveant while maintaining professional boundaries.

I may also help you stay accountable on your healing journey through **compassionate confrontation** by bringing attention to a discrepancy between a behaviour, thought, belief, or choice and the goals or values you shared with me.

At times, I may use **playfulness** as a therapeutic tool. In sessions, humour can help reframe situations, offer a gentle challenge, or bring attention to moments of growth that may feel uncomfortable to acknowledge.

sections.title: Modalities
paragraphs: Because I believe that no two healing journeys are the same, I meet clients where they are and honour their individual pace, needs, and capacity throughout the counselling process.

I take an integrative approach in my counselling work that blends mind-body therapeutic approaches with a particular focus on attachment and the impact of early experiences on our development, and how those experiences may still be impacting our mental wellness in adulthood. Together, we can explore the approaches and strategies that feel most supportive and aligned for you, tailoring counselling to your unique needs.

The therapeutic approaches I typically draw from include:

- Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy (AEDP)
- Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
- Compassion-Focused Therapy
- Internal Family Systems (IFS)
- Motivational Interviewing
- Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT)
- mindfulness
- psychodynamic approaches
